content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or too high after sharp price spikes in history (e.g., 74+ values), then overshoot and fail to correct.
- Model underestimates prices during prolonged downward trends or mean-reversion phases (e.g., 60–65 range).
- Forecast error is more pronounced in the middle of the 30-day window (days 15–25), suggesting lag or insufficient smoothing.
- Model fails to capture true mean reversion toward lower levels after high peaks, especially in 2024-05 data.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values when history includes recent high prices (e.g., 70+), indicating overconfidence in momentum.
- Model underreacts to sudden drops in history (e.g., 60–62 range) and fails to adjust downward quickly.
- Forecast horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are too optimistic in the first 10 days, then too pessimistic in the last 10 days.
